title: Explore the wreck of the Titanic and find ten echoes of her story
author: timcorin
selftext:
Music still drifts down the grand staircase, and the radio room is still sending. Ten small moments from that ship are waiting on the wreck, if you look closely.



It's a slow submersible dive in the browser, desktop or phone, built with Claude Code in Three.js. Claude wrote all the code; I steered by providing screenshots with feedback on my phone and laptop. I also had it pull screenshots from real dive footage of the wreck as reference, and go and find free-to-use rust textures. The music is from Suno. For the look we ran review rounds where Claude agents compared captures against real dive photos of the wreck, a second pass checked each criticism, and only the ones that held up got built.



The hard parts, honestly:



\*\*The rust.\*\* By far the most iteration. Early versions tiled into an obvious grid, then read as camo blotches, then cobblestones, then orange paint chips. What finally worked was structure rather than noise: rust running down along the plate laps, rusticles hanging off the rails, and fog that keeps the unlit hull darker than the water. At one point a run of small additions quietly lost the look I liked, and we had to rebuild it value by value.



\*\*The model.\*\* It needed a lot of cleanup: duplicate faces, the lettering built as geometry (pulling it out left letter-shaped holes in the hull), parts of the superstructure inside out, and an empty hull below C deck with shafts you could dive straight down. Those got sealed off.



\*\*The controls.\*\* A nightmare. I wanted mouse look like an FPS, but in a browser it kept fighting me: pointer lock felt wrong, and macOS was dropping held keys mid-drag. In the end it's keyboard on desktop and a thumbstick on phone, and it's much better for it.
